verdict.rationale: Bento documents an Events API (POST /batch/events) that tracks user activity and explicitly triggers automations. Its workflows start from a trigger and can be built from events, and first-party SDKs in many languages let a product fire these events. missing for 10: explicit documentation that the event payload targets a single subscriber and runs the automation only for that person, documentation of arbitrary custom event names beyond examples like `$purchase`, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can fire a custom event from my product and have it trigger an automation for exactly that person

citations.quote: POST`/batch/events` Create Events Track user activity, update profile fields, and trigger automations.
They capture meaningful user actions with detailed context so you can understand behavior, build better segments, and trigger automations.
Build flows from behavior, events, and tags.
A Workflow is a visual automation that starts with a trigger and executes a series of steps.
Bento has SDKs for JavaScript, Node.js, Next.js, Ruby, PHP, Laravel, WordPress, WooCommerce, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, Swift, Meteor.js, and Supabase.
